record.paper_title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications
record.original_question: How can one- and two-point functions in defect conformal field theory be exploited more fully as input to the boundary conformal bootstrap, and what additional structure of the three-dimensional theory living on the defect must be understood in order to make that program work for the present AdS/dCFT system?

evidence.quote: The idea of using one- and two-point functions as input for the boundary conformal bootstrap equations is only in its infancy. Taking it further would potentially be very interesting but in order to fully exploit it for the present dCFT a better understanding of the 3D theory living on the defect is needed.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a defect conformal field theory (dCFT) in which a codimension-one planar conformal defect (a boundary) breaks the d-dimensional bulk conformal group SO(d,2) down to the subgroup SO(d-1,2) × SO(1) that preserves the defect, so that bulk local operators acquire nonzero one-point functions ⟨O(x)⟩ = a_O / |x_⊥|^{Δ_O} and pairs of bulk operators have two-point functions that depend nontrivially on the conformally invariant cross-ratio constructed from their positions and their distances to the defect. The boundary conformal bootstrap equations express the crossing-symmetry constraint that the two-point function of two bulk operators admits both a bulk operator product expansion (whose coefficients are bulk OPE coefficients times one-point coefficients a_O) and a boundary operator product expansion (whose coefficients are bulk-to-defect couplings of bulk operators to the defect operators of the (d-1)-dimensional conformal theory living on the defect).

Take as the concrete setting the d=4 defect CFT arising from the holographic AdS/dCFT construction in which N=4 super Yang–Mills theory in four dimensions is coupled to a codimension-one defect supporting a three-dimensional conformal field theory, with a nontrivial classical scalar profile producing nonzero one-point functions for a large family of bulk operators.

Problem. Develop a systematic framework in which the known one- and two-point functions of bulk operators serve as input data to the boundary conformal bootstrap equations of this dCFT, and determine what structural data of the three-dimensional conformal field theory localized on the defect (its operator spectrum, defect operator product expansion, bulk-to-defect couplings, and the action of the residual conformal and any preserved supersymmetry on its operators) must be identified in order to close the bootstrap system and extract previously unknown CFT data of the dCFT from it.
artifact.status_search_result: The question concerns an open research direction in the boundary/defect conformal bootstrap program for holographic dCFTs. While progress has been made on the boundary bootstrap and on one-point functions in AdS/dCFT (e.g., works by Kristjansen, de Leeuw and collaborators, and bootstrap studies by Liendo, Meneghelli, Mitev, and others), no complete bootstrap solution incorporating the dCFT one- and two-point function data and the full structure of the 3D defect theory is available. The problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications
status_evidence.snippet: The idea of using one- and two-point functions as input for the boundary conformal bootstrap equations is only in its infancy.
status_evidence.claim: The program is identified as nascent and requires further understanding of the 3D defect theory.
